objects.summary: Owner issues a stale-looking WP2 execution prompt referencing old mission-anchor head ec3f821 despite later durable closure evidence existing on d40053bd.

Codex reconciles current state instead of rebuilding: detects exact independently reviewed d40053bd candidate, reruns 8 WP2 and 29 targeted tests/subtests, makes no code/commit/PR changes and effectively returns NO_CHANGE_REQUIRED.

Owner starts a fresh independent review of exact d40053bd against 13721384, explicitly challenging canonical lineage, sink, executor injection, receipt durability/hash integrity and reuse law without implementation edits.

First independent reviewer returns BLOCK_EVIDENCE because exact base/head are unavailable locally and fetch is 403. No WP2 tests execute and all identities remain UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED; this is evidence-access failure, not substantive contradiction.
Owner relocates independent review to PR #41 whose review head directly descends from exact implementation d40053bd, removing the prior evidence-access blocker while prohibiting implementation edits.

Codex review summary on PR #41 reports completed review with unresolved findings on review head 47e944f, establishing that exact-checkout review found material issues rather than merely repeating prior access failure.

Owner records two independently demonstrated narrow defects on d40053bd. P1: binding never calls runner.execute and verify_bindings alone does not prove execution->evaluation. P2: fixture identity is constructor-cached rather than durably pinned to task before claim/recovery, allowing seed/qualification changes under same task id. Prior PASS is downgraded to REQUEST_CHANGES_NARROW.
Codex review summary confirms completed exact-head review on d40053bd with unresolved findings, aligning with P1/P2 correction requirement.

Owner authorizes only P1/P2 repairs: actual documentary execution plus executed-result validation/identity, and durable task-pinned fixture identity recomputed from consumed inputs on execution/recovery. No scope expansion.

Codex implements P1/P2 locally: runner.execute plus validator_diagnostics_v2, plan/execution/evaluation subject bindings, task-pinned fixture identity and recovery mutation tests. 65 tests plus 29 subtests pass, but push fails because no origin remote; a95d38f remains local only, so no durable PASS is claimed.

Later hosted run on durable d40053bd is blocked only by generated STATE.md freshness (1140 vs 1148 discovered tests); other status/schema/SEC checks pass and full suite is skipped behind the projection gate. Owner scopes continuation to projection freshness only, explicitly separating this repository gate from WP2 semantics.

cross_object_findings.finding: A stale WP2 execution prompt did not trigger reconstruction: Codex reconciled the newer durable reviewed head and returned effectively NO_CHANGE_REQUIRED. This is direct evidence that durable state can prevent restart/rework when consulted.
Issue #40 review spent coordination effort but could only return BLOCK_EVIDENCE because exact objects were inaccessible. It neither supports nor contradicts the existing PASS.

Once the reviewer had exact bytes, it falsified two material claims: no actual execution/evaluation arrow and no durable pre-claim fixture pin. The prior independent PASS was therefore too strong and correctly downgraded to REQUEST_CHANGES_NARROW.

P1 and P2 survived earlier green tests and review rounds, showing that challenge must target semantic claims rather than merely repeat test execution. The counterexamples directly changed the decision.
The P1/P2 correction passed a larger local suite but could not be pushed. Treating a95d38f as remote/durable would repeat the same memory-loss error already observed in WP2 V1.

Hosted CI on the older durable head failed at stale generated STATE.md test count before full suite. The correct action is projection freshness only; this should not be misreported as a WP2 semantic failure.
